datasets.name: ds_metric
queryLines: SELECT campaign_id, campaign_name, week_end, year_adjusted, week_no_adjusted,

columns.description: Selected metric aggregated by its class: ratio metrics as SUM(metric_num)/SUM(metric_denom), Campaign Duration as AVG(metric_num), all others as SUM(metric_num).
columns.expression: CASE WHEN MAX(`metric_class`)='ratio' THEN SUM(`metric_num`)/NULLIF(SUM(`metric_denom`),0) WHEN MAX(`metric_class`)='average' THEN AVG(`metric_num`) ELSE SUM(`metric_num`) END

lines:
## Marketing Campaign Performance — Overview

Scoped to the **last 10 completed weeks** ending 2027-07-31 (the latest week in the data). Counters are pinned to fixed metrics and compare against the prior completed week. The **Metric** filter drives the trend, the five dimension charts, the channel rank and the heatmap — it does not affect the counters, by design.

frame.title: Impressions
frame.description: Sum of metric_num where metric_name = 'Impressions'. Padding rows excluded.

frame.title: Revenue
frame.description: Sum of metric_num. Additive - Revenue's metric_denom is NULL on every row.

frame.title: ROI
frame.description: Total Profit / total Cost - ratio of sums, never an average of ratios.

frame.title: Weekly Trend — selected metric
frame.description: One point per week_end over the 10 completed weeks. Aggregated by the selected metric's class. Gaps are not interpolated.

lines:
### Performance by dimension — selected metric

The same metric and window across five campaign attributes. Best performer first in each chart.

frame.title: Performance by Channel
frame.description: 5 channels. Exempt from nothing - the Channel filter narrows this chart.

frame.title: Performance by Traffic Source
frame.description: 6 traffic sources. Column is named source.

frame.title: Channel Rank by Week
frame.description: DENSE_RANK of the selected metric across the 5 channels each week. 1 = best. Exempt from the Channel filter. A channel with no campaigns in a week has no point - gaps are real, not zeros.

frame.title: Activity Heatmap — Weekday × Week
frame.description: From the daily table. For the four ratio metrics (Conversion Rate, ROI, CPA, Engagement Rate) this plots Conversions instead - they are stored at daily grain as per-campaign ratios and cannot be summed.

lines:
## Campaign Details

One row per campaign over the same 10-week window. Every widget here is **metric-independent** — they count campaigns or measure duration — so the Metric filter does not appear on this page.

frame.title: Campaigns Run
frame.description: COUNT(DISTINCT campaign_id). Padding rows (campaign_id = the literal string 'NULL') are excluded by the view - this is why the all-weeks figure is 1,000 and not 1,001.

frame.title: Avg Campaign Duration
frame.description: AVG of campaign duration in days - an average, never a sum. The padding guard is what separates 49.51 days from 37.39 on the all-weeks figure.

frame.title: Campaign Duration Distribution
frame.description: Distinct campaigns per 10-day duration bin. The bins sum to the Campaigns Run counter.

frame.title: Campaigns by Objective
frame.description: Distinct campaigns per objective. Sums to the Campaigns Run counter.

frame.title: Campaigns by Funnel Stage
frame.description: Distinct campaigns per funnel stage. Sums to the Campaigns Run counter.

frame.title: Campaign Detail
frame.description: One row per campaign, ranked by revenue. Each metric column comes from its own metric_name predicate - never a bare SUM(metric_num).
